movie.title: One Last Throw
movie.overview: Shintaro Yokota, at 18, fulfilled his childhood dream with a dazzling pro debut. Embraced by a loving family and his team, he had a bright career lay ahead—until something felt wrong with his vision. A medical examination delivered a diagnosis no young athlete should ever hear: a brain tumor. Driven by a single desire to play baseball and supported by those who never stopped believing in his comeback, he fought on until his final game, which saw a miracle no one had imagined. The true story of Yokota that continues to move and inspire us all.

aiEnrichment.summary_one_sentence: Faced with a devastating brain tumor diagnosis at the height of his promising young baseball career, Shintaro Yokota fights through immense adversity and visual impairment to deliver one final, unforgettable miraculous play.
aiEnrichment.summary_short: Shintaro Yokota achieved his lifelong dream when he made a stunning professional baseball debut at just 18 years old. However, his promising career was suddenly derailed when trouble with his eyesight led to a tragic brain tumor diagnosis. Supported by his unwavering family and teammates, Yokota endured a grueling battle to return to the sport he loved. His relentless perseverance culminated in a final game where he produced an unimaginable miracle on the field.
aiEnrichment.summary_long: Shintaro Yokota was an exceptionally talented 18-year-old athlete who captured the hearts of fans during his dazzling professional baseball debut. With the unwavering support of a loving family and dedicated teammates, he seemed destined for a long and brilliant career in the sports world. Tragically, this bright future was thrown into turmoil when Yokota began experiencing persistent issues with his vision. A comprehensive medical examination confirmed every young athlete's worst nightmare: a life-threatening brain tumor. Forced off the field, Yokota began a long and arduous medical fight, anchored by a singular, burning desire to play baseball again. Throughout his painful treatment and recovery process, his loved ones and team refused to lose faith in his eventual comeback. Yokota worked tirelessly to overcome severe physical limitations and impaired eyesight just to put on his uniform one last time. During his final appearance on the field, Yokota delivered a breathtaking, miraculous play that surpassed anything anyone could have imagined. His extraordinary journey remains a profound, true story of resilience, hope, and unwavering spirit that continues to inspire audiences worldwide.
aiEnrichment.synopsis: One Last Throw tells the poignant true story of Shintaro Yokota, an extraordinarily gifted 18-year-old baseball prodigy whose promising professional career is abruptly halted by a life-altering brain tumor diagnosis. As his world is turned upside down, Yokota refuses to surrender his dream of returning to the diamond. Guided by the boundless love of his family, the loyalty of his teammates, and an indomitable spirit, he embarks on an emotional battle against illness to stand on the field once more.

faq.answer: Shintaro Yokota was an 18-year-old high school prodigy drafted by the Hanshin Tigers in 2013 who made a promising pro debut before being diagnosed with a brain tumor at age 21.
faq.question: Who was Shintaro Yokota in real life?

faq.answer: Rookie actor Takaya Matsutani stars as Shintaro Yokota, performing alongside veteran actors Kyoka Suzuki and Katsunori Takahashi.
faq.question: Who plays the lead role of Shintaro Yokota?

faq.answer: The film was directed, planned, and produced by Japanese filmmaker Jun Akiyama.
faq.question: Who directed One Last Throw?

faq.answer: The miracle refers to Yokota's legendary 'miraculous back home' throw from center field directly to the catcher during his final retirement game in 2019, despite severely impaired vision.
faq.question: What is the 'miracle' featured in the story?

faq.answer: Yes, the film draws heavily from Yokota's own autobiography, 'The Miracle Back Home,' as well as the non-fiction book 'The Glorious Back Home: Yokota Shintaro, Eternal Number 24' by Yuriko Nakai.
